text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 1.6% today, continuing a sharp two-week rally of 22.6%. The driver is clear: escalating Middle East tensions have pushed global crude oil prices to $125 per barrel (a 30% jump over the US domestic price), while refinery utilization sits at 92.7%—near full capacity. When crude prices spike and refineries are running hard, refiners' profit margins typically widen because they can pass costs through faster than their input expenses rise. News of Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities directly threatened global oil supply on today's trading session, lifting the entire sector.

The tightness is expected to persist: the International Energy Agency warned that diesel supplies will remain constrained well into 2027 due to the Iran conflict, falling inventories, and strong demand. For a refiner like this one, sustained high crude prices coupled with tight product inventories and full utilization rates creates an extended window of favorable economics.
